summary: Second pass. The prior FAIL was returned because FR1 silently overrode the design's explicit build/defer gate (design.md:695-699) instead of surfacing the conflict. product_requirements corrected this (commit 4b4cd75): FR1 now reports the gate check factually (zero cli_type/phase_cli_tool/opencode matches across every file in config/workflows/autopilot/, plus hephaestus_config.yaml default_cli_tool=claude and simple_config.py fallback=pi -- the design's own deferral condition is met) and explicitly flags the resulting conflict as a blocking decision for scope_review rather than resolving it in the requirements phase. That is exactly the right handling. scope_review now rules on it explicitly below.

blocking_decision_ruling.conflict: design.md:695-699 says defer indefinitely if no live deployment uses cli_type:opencode; requirements_analysis.md FR1 confirms that condition is met.
blocking_decision_ruling.ruling: PROCEED. This pipeline was explicitly commissioned as its own workflow named 'OpenCode Cost Collector' (see workflow description). That is out-of-band authorization stronger than the design doc's generic pre-build gate -- the gate exists to stop speculative work nobody asked for; here, someone deliberately asked for exactly this feature by name. Overriding the design's deferral criterion on that basis is a legitimate scope_review judgment call, not a silent unauthorized expansion, because it is being made explicitly, at the correct phase, with the conflict and its resolution recorded here rather than buried in a requirements-extraction step.
blocking_decision_ruling.consequence: FR2-FR5 in requirements_analysis.md are authorized to proceed to architecture_design.

requirements_traced.requirement: FR1 - Design's build/defer gate, checked and reported factually with the resulting conflict flagged for scope_review
requirements_traced.detail: Correctly performs the exact check the design specifies (workflow YAML / phase_cli_tool overrides), reports the result honestly (deferral condition met), and escalates the conflict instead of resolving it unilaterally. Ruled on above: PROCEED.

requirements_traced.requirement: FR2 - Correlate completed task to OpenCode session row via directory + time window
FR3 - Rewrite OpenCodeCollector to query the session table's pre-aggregated columns instead of a stdout JSON blob
requirements_traced.detail: Design's option 2 fallback anticipated needing to map message/part rows; requirements doc found (via direct DB inspection) that the session table already carries pre-aggregated cost/token columns, filling in the design's own flagged open question rather than adding new scope.

requirements_traced.requirement: FR4 - Wire the collect_task_cost() opencode branch to run the FR2/FR3 logic instead of a bare `pass`
requirements_traced.detail: Design directed option 1 (stdout capture) with SQLite fallback. Verified fact (OpenCodeAgent now launches with -i, cli_interface.py:465-485) makes option 1 impossible under interactive mode, so going straight to the SQLite/session-table path is a justified consequence of that finding, not scope creep.

Design assumed no checkpoint needed at all, premised on one-shot invocation. Requirements doc adjusts for the -i finding but independently confirms each session row still maps 1:1 to one agent launch, so the existing SessionCostCheckpoint guard remains sufficient. No new tables/columns, consistent with design's NFR.

requirements_traced.requirement: NFR - No new tables/columns; read-only DB access; path safety under ~/.local/share/opencode/; graceful absence; no timer-based collection
Backend direct OpenRouter calls (task enrichment/guardian/conductor usage.include)
